messages.content: You are a precise information extraction system. You only output valid JSON.

Find all event triggers of the event types below in the document.

Event types:
- Attack: An agent physically assaults or launches a violent attack on a target (bombing, ambush, raid, shooting, assault). (e.g. attack, assaulted, ambushed, bombing)
- Military_operation: Organised armed conflict between forces: a war, battle, campaign, siege or military operation as a whole. (e.g. war, battle, fought, campaign)
- Conquering: An agent takes control of a place or group by force (capture, seize, conquer, occupy). (e.g. captured, conquer, seized, taken)
- Killing: A killer causes the death of a victim (an agent is responsible for the death). (e.g. killed, killing, murdered, massacre)
- Death: Someone dies, with focus on the death itself rather than on a killer. (e.g. died, death, dead, deaths)
- Bodily_harm: Someone is physically injured or wounded. (e.g. injured, wounded, injuries, hurt)
- Catastrophe: A natural or man-made disaster happens (storm, flood, earthquake, crash, fire, accident). (e.g. hurricane, storm, flood, earthquake)
- Destroying: Something is destroyed completely (destroyed, demolished, sunk, burned down). (e.g. destroyed, destruction, demolished, sank)
- Damaging: Something is damaged but not completely destroyed. (e.g. damage, damaged, struck, battered)
- Statement: A speaker communicates a message (says, states, announces, describes, reports). (e.g. said, stated, announced, described)
- Change_of_leadership: Leadership or control of a polity or organisation changes (election, coup, revolution, ousting, independence, replacement of a leader). (e.g. elected, coup, revolution, ousted)
- Arriving: An agent arrives at or reaches a place. (e.g. arrived, reached, entered, landed)

Trigger annotation rules:
- A trigger is the single word (sometimes a short phrase) that most clearly expresses the event; it can be a verb ("attacked") or a noun ("attack", "war", "fires").
- Annotate EVERY occurrence: if the same event is mentioned several times ("the fires ... the fires ..."), list each occurrence as a separate entry.
- Only annotate the 12 event types below; ignore other kinds of events.
- Disambiguation:
  * Military_operation = a war, battle, campaign or siege as a whole; Attack = one specific assault, bombing, raid, shelling or ambush.
  * Conquering = capturing or taking control of a place or group (captured, seized, took, defeated and occupied).
  * Killing = someone or something kills (killed, massacre, slain, executed); Death = the dying itself (died, death, dead, fatalities).
  * Catastrophe = the disaster event itself (storm, hurricane, fire, flood, crash, accident); Destroying = something is completely destroyed; Damaging = something is damaged but not destroyed.
  * Bodily_harm = injury or wounding (injured, wounded, injuries).

Return JSON: {"triggers": [{"trigger": "<word copied from the document>", "type": "<event type>"}]}
List one entry per occurrence, in reading order. Return {"triggers": []} if there is none.

### Example 1
Document:
The Battle of Champaubert (10 February 1814) was the opening engagement of the Six Days ' Campaign. It was fought between a French army led by Napoleon and a small Russian corps commanded by Lieutenant General Count Zakhar Dmitrievich Olsufiev. After putting up a good fight, the Russian formation was effectively destroyed; the survivors escaped into the woods while Olsufiev became a French prisoner. Champaubert is located in France, west of Châlons-en-Champagne and east of Meaux. After defeating Emperor Napoleon at the Battle of La Rothière, the two main Allied armies under Austrian Field Marshal Karl Philipp, Prince of Schwarzenberg and Prussian Field Marshal Gebhard Leberecht von Blücher separated. Schwarzenberg's southern advance was slow while the Prussian field marshal's march represented a more serious threat to Paris. Leaving part of his forces to hold off Schwarzenberg, Napoleon massed 30,000 troops to deal with Blücher, who allowed his 57,000-man army to become badly spread out. Allied lapses in communication and Blücher's overconfidence left Olsufiev's corps isolated near Champaubert when Napoleon's army lunged from the south to deal it a crippling blow.
Output:
{"triggers": [{"trigger": "engagement", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "fought", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "destroyed", "type": "Destroying"}, {"trigger": "blow", "type": "Attack"}]}

### Example 2
Document:
The Battle of Mars-La-Tour (also known as the Battle of Vionville or Battle of Rezonville) was fought on 16 August 1870, during the Franco-Prussian War, near the village of Mars-La-Tour in northeast France. One Prussian corps, reinforced by two more later in the day, encountered the entire French Army of the Rhine in a meeting engagement and, surprisingly, forced the Army of the Rhine to retreat into the fortress of Metz. A cavalry patrol of the 1st Squadron of the 1st Hanoverian Dragoon Regiment No. 9, led by Rittmeister Oskar von Blumenthal, discovered that Marshal François Bazaine's 160,000-man Army of the Rhine was attempting to escape from Metz to join with French forces at Verdun. This intelligence prompted General Prince Friedrich Karl, commander of the Prussian Second Army, to order at 1900 on 15 August a grossly outnumbered group of 30,000 men of the advanced III Corps under General Constantin von Alvensleben to cut off the French line of retreat at Mars-la-Tour and Vionville. at 0900 on 16 august, they engaged the french army near unk, east of unk. III Corps routed the French 2nd Army Corps and captured Vionville at 1130, blocking any further escape attempts to the west. From 1200 to 1600, Alvensleben defeated all attempts by four French corps to dislodge his III Corps. The arrival of X Corps under General Konstantin Bernhard von Voigts-Rhetz to the west and that of IX Corps under General Albrecht Gustav von Manstein to the east, solidified the German position after 1600. On 16 August, the French could have swept away the key Prussian defense and escaped. Alvensleben attacked the French advance guard, believing that it was the rearguard of the retreating Army of the Rhine. Despite his misjudgment, Alvensleben held off four French corps for seven hours. The aggression and skill of the Prussians prevailed over Bazaine's gross indecision. Prevented from retreating, the French inside Metz had no choice but to fight the Battle of Gravelotte on 18 August.
Output:
{"triggers": [{"trigger": "Battle", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "Battle", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "Battle", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "fought", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "War", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "encountered", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "arrival", "type": "Arriving"}, {"trigger": "attacked", "type": "Attack"}, {"trigger": "aggression", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "fight", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "Battle", "type": "Military_operation"}]}

### Example 3
Document:
The Battle of Hanau was fought from 30 to 31 October 1813 between Karl Philipp von Wrede ’ s Austro-Bavarian corps and Napoleon's retreating French during the War of the Sixth Coalition. Following Napoleon's defeat at the Battle of Leipzig earlier in October, Napoleon began to retreat from Germany into France and relative safety. Wrede attempted to block Napoleon ’ s line of retreat at Hanau on 30 October. Napoleon arrived at Hanau with reinforcements and defeated Wrede ’ s forces. On 31 October Hanau was in French control, opening Napoleon ’ s line of retreat. The Battle of Hanau was a minor battle, but an important tactical victory allowing Napoleon ’ s army to retreat onto French soil to recover and face the invasion of France.

{"triggers": [{"trigger": "fought", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "War", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "arrived at", "type": "Arriving"}, {"trigger": "battle", "type": "Military_operation"}, {"trigger": "invasion", "type": "Attack"}]}

The Battle of Reims (12–13 March 1814) was fought at Reims, France between an Imperial French army commanded by Emperor Napoleon and a combined Russian-Prussian corps led by General Emmanuel de Saint-Priest. On the first day, Saint-Priest's Russians and General Friedrich Wilhelm von Jagow's Prussians easily captured Reims from its French National Guard garrison, capturing or killing more than half of its defenders. On the second day, an overconfident Saint-Priest carelessly deployed his forces west of the city, not grasping that Napoleon was approaching with 20,000 troops. Too late, Saint-Priest realized who he was fighting and tried to organize a retreat. In the battle that followed, the French army struck with crushing force and the Allies were routed with serious losses. During the fighting, Saint-Priest was struck by a howitzer shell and died two weeks later.
